surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Clarke plays hero in overtime
paras: Artemi Panarin struck first for the Kings early in the first, and he scored again late in the period to make it 2-0. Logan Stanley and Samuel Helenius fought later in the period. Semyon Varlamov stopped Adrian Kempe on a penalty shot midway through the second. Victor Eklund got the Islanders on the board on the power play later in the period, and Matthew Schaefer tied it up early in the third. Brandt Clarke won it less than three minutes into overtime.

The Islanders outshot the Kings 43-27, but the Kings’ looks were better, so the chances came out about even. Darcy Kuemper made 41 saves for the Kings. By our Swing measure, Emil Heineman had the best night of anyone, even in a loss and with Clarke’s overtime winner in the game. The Kings moved to 2-4-2 and climbed to sixth in the Pacific, while the Isles fell to 5-3-2, third in the Metropolitan.

items.text: The Islanders have points in five straight games (3-0-2).
The Kings have beaten the Islanders six straight times, going back to the 2023-24 season.
Matthew Schaefer scored his first goal of the season, his first since Apr 9 (twelve games played since).
Quinton Byfield was in NHL.com’s projected lineup, but Jared Wright played instead.
